 Nearly 1.6M pounds of hot dogs, bacon and other meats recalled nationwide
 The USDA's FSIS gave the recall its highest classification, warning of possible serious health consequences or death
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Threads 
 Print 
 Email 
 Add Fox Business on Google 
 By Landon Mion FOXBusiness close video FOX Business Flash top headlines for October 19 
 Check out what's clicking on FoxBusiness.com.
 Nearly 1.6 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry products, including hot dogs, bacon, brisket and ham, are facing a recall over potential "temperature abuse" during storage, according to federal officials.
 Kayem Foods Inc. issued a voluntary recall for about 1,584,361 pounds of ready-to-eat food items, the Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) announced over the weekend.
 FSIS gave the recall its highest-level classification, meaning there is a "reasonable probability" that consuming the affected products could cause "serious, adverse health consequences or death."
 CHEDDAR CHEESE RECALLED ACROSS SEVERAL STATES OVER DANGEROUS E. COLI 
 Nearly 1.6 million pounds of ready-to-eat meat and poultry products are facing a recall. (USDA) 
 The meat and poultry products were shipped to retail and foodservice locations across the country, as well as to Hong Kong.
 The affected items were produced approximately from March 31 through Oct. 7. The products bear establishment numbers "EST. M/P 7839," "EST. P 20935A" and "EST. M 9520" inside the USDA mark of inspection.
 Kayem Foods Inc. has provided a nine-page list of all the affected items, which includes Kayem Beef & Pork Hot Dogs, Kayem Double Smoked Thick Cut Bacon, Kayem Slow Smoked Beef Brisket, Genoa Hot Ham, Al Fresco Roasted Pepper & Asiago Chicken Sausage and Triple M Boneless Ham Steaks.
 Kayem Foods Inc. issued a voluntary recall for about 1,584,361 pounds of ready-to-eat food items. (USDA) 
 The problem was discovered after the company received a retail customer complaint about warm product temperatures at the point of delivery on October 1.
 The firm investigated the complaint and determined that they stored various ready-to-eat meat and poultry products in a warehouse cooler that experienced temperature deviations.
 Kayem said the temperature deviations resulted from a cooling-system malfunction at one of its warehouses. The company said it has corrected the issue and is conducting the recall out of an abundance of caution.
 MORE THAN 82K RECHARGEABLE HAND WARMERS RECALLED OVER FIRE RISK 
 There have been no confirmed reports of illness linked to the consumption of these products. (J. David Ake/Getty Images / Getty Images) 
 There have been no confirmed reports of illness linked to the consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an illness is urged to contact a healthcare provider.
 CLICK HERE TO GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO 
 FSIS said it is concerned that some affected items may be in consumers’ refrigerators.
 Consumers who have purchased these products are directed not to consume them and to instead throw them away or return them to the place of purchase .
